Posted November 15, 2007 

Analysis by Richard Cowan  

 

Even people who completely disagree with John McCain on many issues respect him as a brave man who endured years of torture and abuse as a POW in North Viet Nam. And that is certainly his due, but there have been brave men on all sides in all wars, even amongst our worst enemies.  

 

Physical courage does not imply wisdom, or even moral courage.  

 

Thus, I respect John McCain for what he was, but I have contempt for what he has become. 

 

I am forced to this conclusion because I have known too many other prisoners who have suffered at the hands of a government whose policies are supported by John McCain. 

 

I have written a lot about Steve Tuck, who nearly died while a prisoner of the drug war in Washington. Like McCain, he is a disabled veteran, but he is still being denied the medical care to which he is entitled. 

See 

Steve Tuck Was Held In Whatcom County Jail WITHOUT MORPHINE! He Is In Agony! Case to Be Federalized, But We Won't Know Until Tuesday. His Life Is In Danger.  

See 

Of course, there are many others who are simply prisoners of their own bodies, and have to escape the torture of being denied their medicine by committing suicide. 

See
The Murder of Robin Prosser. An Indictment of Karen Tandy and Motorola By Their Own Words and Standards. 
 

Senator McCain has rightly spoken out against the torture of suspected terrorists in Guantanamo and in Iraq, and he has been rightly praised for that by civil rights activists and the anti-war movement. However, by their silence they have become as complicit as he is in the torture of people in pain. 

 

Last night I saw a perfect example of the blindness of the Progressive left on Keith Olbermann's Countdown on MSNBC, which I enjoy even when I disagree. 

 

Olbermann was indignant about McCain's laughing at a question in which Hillary Clinton was called a bitch and said that McCain should have reprimanded the questioner. Okay. 

 

However, no one on the left seems to have noticed McCain's callous dismissal of medical cannabis. Why is McCain's failing to denounce rudeness to a politician worse than the Progressives failure to denounce his callous and profoundly anti-democratic opposition to medical marijuana? 

See
Drug Warrior John Edwards Gets Endorsement of Ex-Hippy Turned Hip Capitalist, Ice Cream Magnate, Ben Cohen. The Sixties Never Happened. 

I found the story this morning on two libertarian sites, Jonathan Rick's No Straw Men blog and on Reasons Hit and Runwhich isn't too surprising, but also on the Conservative American Spectator, which also indicates how politically out of touch McCain has become.  

 

The question should have been easy for a true conservative who believes in federalism: "Should federal law supersede the will of the people in a given state when it comes to medical marijuana?" 

 

From the American Spectator: 

 

McCain: "The will of the people, my friend, is that medical marijuana is not something that the quote 'people' want," he responded. "Certain people feel strongly about this issue, and they show up at most town hall meetings, obviously feel very strongly about it. There is no convincing evidence there's evidence, but no convincing evidence to me that medical marijuana relief of pain and suffering cannot be accomplished by prescriptions from doctors So, when you're talking about the will of the people, you're going to have to show me the will of the people besides the will of a small number of people who feel very strongly about the issue, as obviously you do." 

 

The questioner mentioned that voters approved of medical marijuana in a California referendum. 

 

"There may be times when the will of the people, for example Iraq, the will of the people, unfortunately is that we withdraw from Iraq immediately or very very soon," McCain shot back. "I don't share that view of the will of the people." 

 

I think he will soon have other occasions when he will not share that view of the will of the people.
